failure.cause: Windows default cp1252 decoding of the UTF-8 fixture produced a different UTF-8 string hash from the saved source. The reader correctly rejected that source identity before reaching the intended boundary mutation. Controlled cp1252/LF reproduces the exact error; UTF-8/LF and UTF-8/CRLF both reach the intended boundary error because this historical reader normalizes newlines.
failure.correction: The test now reads/writes explicit UTF-8 and LF, then signs the actual saved bytes. Production identity verification is unchanged.
failure.initial_diagnosis_corrected: The first line-ending diagnosis was disproved by the controlled simulation. The codepage is the reproducing cause; the fixture correction explicitly fixes both encoding and line endings.
